Making the Dutch scholarly corpus global, open and resilient

Dutch university libraries, the KB National Library, SURF and OpenAIRE work together on a shared, mature and resilient infrastructure for Dutch scientific output. Together we reinforce the Netherlands Research Portal and the landscape of institutional repositories and CRIS systems, so that Dutch research output is more robust, sovereign and findable.

Key figures

  • 15 cooperation partners support DURF in kind
  • 3.4 million records in the Dutch Scholarly Communication Corpus
  • 66.8% of the publications in Dutch CRIS systems have no file
  • 22 of 86 Dutch repositories and CRIS systems in OpenAIRE meet the current guidelines
  • Unknown files backed up in the KB e-Depot
  • Unknown visitors of the Netherlands Research Portal

Sources: cooperation partners from section 4.2 of the DURF full proposal. Records: published works in the Netherlands Research Portal, as cited in the position paper. Missing files: 66.8% of 1,912,504 publications, DURF Full Text Monitor, snapshot of the SURF ORI DuckLake loaded 4 March 2026. Guidelines: CRIS v1.1 or Literature v4.0, OpenAIRE APIs on 3 November 2026, DURF Metadata Monitor. e-Depot files and portal visitors are not yet measured.

Together, the libraries are the custodians of the Dutch Scholarly Communication Corpus.

Taking care of a valuable shared common resource: the Dutch scholarly communication corpus

The Dutch Repository Federation (DURF) is a four-year programme, from 1 June 2026 to 31 May 2030, in which Dutch university libraries, the KB National Library, SURF and OpenAIRE work together on a shared, mature and resilient infrastructure for Dutch scientific output.

DURF reinforces the Netherlands Research Portal and the institutional repository and CRIS landscape, so that Dutch research output is more robust, sovereign and findable. Six themes run in parallel over the four years.

Together, the libraries are the custodians of the Dutch Scholarly Communication Corpus. The position paper explains why that matters and what the signatories commit to.

  • Read the position paper
  • Visit the portal

One federation, six themes

The six themes run in parallel from June 2026 to May 2030. Each has its own colour, which you will find back in the roadmap and the dashboards. Goals and partners follow the project roadmap; the people behind each theme are in our team.

Governance of the Federation and Netherlands Research Portal

A sustainable governance framework for the Dutch federated research information ecosystem, including the parties that maintain repository and CRIS systems, the e-Depot and the OpenAIRE Graph.

Leads: Simone Kortekaas (KB National Library) and Maurice Vanderfeesten (SURF).
Partners: SURF (community management, legal advice, project assistance).

Metadata Quality Improvement

Repository and CRIS systems adopt the updated metadata and exchange standards for high-quality research metadata that comply with international guidelines and meet national requirements.

Lead: Rutger de Jong (Leiden University).
Partners: WUR (tech lead), SURF (community management, legal advice, project assistance, architect), KB (WISH).

Full Text Capture

Comprehensive full-text availability in Dutch repository and CRIS systems, primarily for preservation, and secondarily for text mining, AI usage and Taverne mechanisms.

Lead: Pascal Braak (University of Amsterdam).
Partners: WUR (tech lead), SURF (community management, legal advice, project assistance).

KB National Library e-Depot Archiving

Comprehensive preservation of Dutch scientific output in the KB e-Depot.

Lead: Ingeborg Verheul (KB National Library).
Partners: WUR (tech lead), SURF (legal).

Metadata Distribution & Discovery Optimization

Increase the visibility of Dutch research content in major international indexes.

Lead: Rutger de Jong (Leiden University).
Partners: WUR (tech lead).

NL Research Portal Update

A fully functional, user-centred Netherlands Research Portal that serves as the primary discovery point for Dutch research output.

Lead: vacant.
Partners: none listed yet.

The people behind DURF

DURF is run by people from the university libraries, the KB National Library, SURF and OpenAIRE. The project lead and the theme leads coordinate the work, supporting roles keep it running, and a steering group oversees it on behalf of the partners.

Announcements, newest first

Open an item to read it; a link can open one straight away, like this one to the DURF Federation Day.

DURF Federation Day

18 November 2026

On Wednesday 18 November, from 12:00 to 17:00, the first DURF Federation Day takes place at SURF Utrecht, room 2.03. We invite all DURF co-applicants, cooperation partners and Chiefs Open Science to work together on making the Dutch scientific corpus open, available and resilient, within the existing infrastructure and organisational structures.

The proposal was submitted with your help in early 2025, we received the green light at the end of 2025, the project officially started on 1 June and the kick-off with the core group took place on 23 September. Now it is time to involve the cooperation partners, the Chiefs Open Science and other stakeholders. This day is the first in a series spread over the next four years.

We will inform you about the thematic objectives and the activities we coordinate to achieve them, and about how each institution can contribute in concrete terms. Because areas of interest and expertise differ between institutions, we use the day to establish who can contribute to what. This concerns first of all the in-kind contribution during the project period, but we will also address our shared responsibility for maintaining the infrastructure after 2030 and continuing to benefit from it.

Programme: lunch at 12:00, programme starts at 13:00, drinks at 16:00. Registration is required because of room capacity and dietary requirements.

Metadata Monitor and Full Text Monitor online

November 2026

The first two DURF dashboards are online as proofs of concept: the Metadata Monitor (theme 2) and the Full Text Monitor (theme 3). They show real figures from a static snapshot of the SURF ORI DuckLake catalog and the OpenAIRE APIs. Charts can be embedded in other pages.

Position paper (draft)

October 2026

The draft position paper is published: a call for Dutch university libraries to commit to a shared infrastructure for Dutch scientific output. Comments are welcome via the source on GitHub.

Data governance and the project roadmap

September 2026

The draft data contracts page describes how every party in the federation can deliver its data as a product, according to a contract. The project roadmap was updated with the six themes, their activities and months.

From proposal to federation

The roadmap shows the activities of each theme per month.

  • Early 2025 Proposal submitted, with the help of the Dutch libraries
  • End 2025 Green light for the project
  • 1 Jun 2026 Project start
  • 23 Sep 2026 Kick-off with the core group
  • 18 Nov 2026 First DURF Federation Day, at SURF Utrecht
  • 31 May 2030 Project end
